theory.overview: Hash tables (hash maps) provide $O(1)$ average-case lookup, insert, and delete by mapping keys to array indices using a hash function. The core idea: compute hash(key) → index, store value at that index. When collisions occur (multiple keys map to same index), use collision resolution (chaining or open addressing). Hash tables are ubiquitous—used in databases, caches, symbol tables, and many algorithms. Understanding hash functions, collision resolution, and load factor is crucial for effective use.

sections.title: Hash Functions
sections.content: A good hash function distributes keys uniformly across indices, minimizes collisions, and is fast to compute. Properties: deterministic (same key → same hash), uniform distribution, avalanche effect (small input change → large output change). Common functions: division method (hash = key % m), multiplication method (hash = floor(m * (key * A mod 1))), universal hashing (random function from family). For strings: polynomial rolling hash: hash = Σ(s[i] × p^i) mod m.
properties: Deterministic: same key always produces same hash
Uniform distribution: keys spread evenly across buckets
Fast computation: O(1) time to compute
Avalanche effect: small input change → large output change

sections.title: Collision Resolution
sections.content: Chaining: each bucket is a linked list of key-value pairs. When collision, add to list. Lookup: hash to bucket, traverse list. Load factor α = n/m (n elements, m buckets). With chaining, expected chain length = α. Open addressing: all elements stored in array. On collision, probe next slot (linear, quadratic, double hashing). Linear probing: next = (hash + i) % m. Quadratic: next = (hash + c1×i + c2×i²) % m. Double hashing: next = (hash + i×hash2(key)) % m.

sections.title: Load Factor and Resizing
sections.content: Load factor α = n/m (elements / buckets). As α increases, collisions increase, performance degrades. For chaining, α > 1 means average chain > 1. For open addressing, α must be < 1. When α exceeds threshold (typically 0.7-0.75), resize: allocate larger array (usually 2×), rehash all elements. Resizing is $O(n)$ but amortized $O(1)$ per operation. Choosing good initial size and threshold balances memory and performance.

sections.title: Hash Table Applications
sections.content: Caching: LRU cache uses hash map + doubly linked list. Symbol tables: compilers use hash tables for variable lookup. Databases: hash indexes for fast key lookup. Counting/frequency: count occurrences of elements. Two-sum problem: find pair summing to target. Grouping: group anagrams, group by category. Deduplication: remove duplicates from collection.

sections.title: Hash Table vs Other Structures
sections.content: Hash table: $O(1)$ average lookup/insert/delete, no order, requires hashable keys. Binary search tree: $O(\log n)$ lookup/insert/delete, maintains order, no hash function needed. Array: $O(1)$ index access, $O(n)$ search, ordered. Linked list: $O(n)$ search, ordered, dynamic size. Choose hash table for fast lookups when order doesn't matter.

keyConcepts.name: Hash Function
keyConcepts.description: Maps key to bucket index. Must be deterministic, fast, and distribute uniformly. Poor hash function → many collisions → poor performance.

keyConcepts.name: Collision
keyConcepts.description: Two different keys hash to same index. Inevitable due to pigeonhole principle (infinite keys, finite buckets). Resolution strategies: chaining or open addressing.
keyConcepts.pigeonhole: More keys than buckets guarantees collisions

keyConcepts.name: Load Factor
keyConcepts.description: α = n/m. Measures how full hash table is. Higher α = more collisions = slower operations. Resize when α exceeds threshold.
keyConcepts.threshold: Typically 0.7-0.75 for chaining, 0.5-0.7 for open addressing

keyConcepts.name: Rehashing
keyConcepts.description: When resizing, compute new hash for all elements using new bucket count. Required because hash depends on bucket count.
keyConcepts.cost: $O(n)$ for all elements, amortized $O(1)$ per operation

steps.title: Compute Hash
steps.description: Apply hash function to key: index = hash(key) % capacity.

steps.title: Check Collision
steps.description: Check if bucket at index is empty. If empty, insert. If occupied, handle collision.
steps.code: if buckets[index] == null: insert; else: resolve_collision();

steps.title: Resolve Collision (Chaining)
steps.description: Add to linked list at bucket. If key exists, update value. Else append new node.
steps.code: node = buckets[index]; while node: if node.key == key: update; node = node.next; append;

steps.title: Resize if Needed
steps.description: If load factor > threshold, resize to 2× capacity, rehash all elements.

steps.title: Return
steps.description: Return inserted/updated value or found value for lookup.

practiceProblems.title: Two Sum
practiceProblems.description: Find two numbers that sum to target in array.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map: value → index. For each num, check if target - num in map. If yes, return indices. Else add num to map.

practiceProblems.title: Valid Anagram
practiceProblems.description: Check if two strings are anagrams using hash map.
practiceProblems.solution: Count characters in s. Decrement for t. If any count non-zero, not anagram. Or use array of size 26.

practiceProblems.title: Group Anagrams
practiceProblems.description: Group anagrams together from array of strings.
practiceProblems.solution: For each string, sort characters to get key. Hash map: key → list of strings. Return all values.
hints: Or use character count as key

practiceProblems.title: Top K Frequent Elements
practiceProblems.description: Return k most frequent elements in array.
practiceProblems.solution: Count frequencies with hash map. Use min-heap of size k to keep top k. Or bucket sort by frequency.
hints: Min-heap of size k for top k

practiceProblems.title: Product of Array Except Self
practiceProblems.description: Return array where output[i] = product of all elements except nums[i].
practiceProblems.solution: Two passes: left products and right products. Or single pass with running product and hash map.

practiceProblems.title: Longest Consecutive Sequence
practiceProblems.description: Find length of longest consecutive elements sequence.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash set of all numbers. For each number, if num-1 not in set, it's sequence start. Count consecutive numbers. Track max.
hints: Only start counting from sequence starts

practiceProblems.title: Isomorphic Strings
practiceProblems.description: Check if two strings are isomorphic (characters can be replaced to get other).
practiceProblems.solution: Two hash maps: s→t and t→s. Check mappings are consistent. No two characters map to same character.
hints: Two hash maps for bidirectional mapping
No two characters map to same

practiceProblems.title: Word Pattern
practiceProblems.description: Check if string follows pattern (pattern='abba', str='dog cat cat dog' → true).
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map: pattern char → word. Check consistency. Also ensure no two pattern chars map to same word.

practiceProblems.title: Find Duplicate Number
practiceProblems.description: Find duplicate in array of n+1 integers where each is 1 to n.
practiceProblems.solution: Floyd's cycle detection (treat array as linked list). Or use hash set (O(n) space).
hints: Treat as linked list: index → value

practiceProblems.title: Contains Duplicate II
practiceProblems.description: Check if two distinct indices i,j with nums[i]==nums[j] and |i-j|≤k.
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window with hash set. Maintain set of last k elements. If current in set, return true.

practiceProblems.title: Contains Duplicate III
practiceProblems.description: Check if i,j with |i-j|≤k and |nums[i]-nums[j]|≤t.
practiceProblems.solution: Sliding window with ordered set (TreeSet). For each element, check if any in window within t range.

practiceProblems.title: LRU Cache
practiceProblems.description: Implement LRU cache with get and put operations.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map + doubly linked list. Map key → node. DLL maintains access order (MRU at head, LRU at tail).
hints: MRU at head, LRU at tail

practiceProblems.title: Insert Delete GetRandom O(1)
practiceProblems.description: Design data structure with insert, delete, getRandom in O(1).
practiceProblems.solution: Array + hash map. Array stores values. Hash map: value → index. Delete: swap with last, update map, pop last.
hints: Swap with last for O(1) deletion

practiceProblems.title: Design Twitter
practiceProblems.description: Design simplified Twitter with postTweet, getNewsFeed, follow, unfollow.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map: user → tweets (list) and following. For feed, merge tweets from followees using heap.
hints: Merge k sorted lists for feed

practiceProblems.title: Random Pick Index
practiceProblems.description: Given array with possible duplicates, pick random index of target.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map: value → list of indices. Pick random from list. Or reservoir sampling (O(1) space).

practiceProblems.title: Design Underground System
practiceProblems.description: Track customer travel times between stations.
practiceProblems.solution: Two hash maps: customer → (station, time) and station pair → (total time, count).

practiceProblems.title: First Unique Character
practiceProblems.description: Find first non-repeating character in string.
practiceProblems.solution: Two passes: first count characters, second find first with count 1. Or use ordered hash map.

practiceProblems.title: Subarray Sum Equals K
practiceProblems.description: Find number of subarrays summing to k.
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map: prefix sum → count. For each prefix sum, check if prefix - k in map. Add count to result.

practiceProblems.title: Contiguous Array
practiceProblems.description: Find max length subarray with equal number of 0s and 1s.
practiceProblems.solution: Treat 0 as -1. Track prefix sum. Hash map: sum → first index. When sum repeats, subarray between has equal 0s and 1s.
hints: When sum repeats, subarray is valid

practiceProblems.title: Longest Harmonious Subsequence
practiceProblems.description: Find longest subsequence where max - min = 1.
practiceProblems.solution: Count frequencies with hash map. For each value, check if value+1 exists. Sum frequencies of value and value+1.
hints: Sum frequencies of value and value+1

practiceProblems.title: Maximum Size Subarray Sum Equals k
practiceProblems.description: Find max length subarray summing to k.
practiceProblems.solution: Prefix sum with hash map. Map: sum → earliest index. When sum - k found, update max length.
hints: Update max length when sum - k found

practiceProblems.title: Find the Difference
practiceProblems.description: Find added character in t (t is s shuffled plus one char).
practiceProblems.solution: XOR all characters. Result is the extra character. Or count characters.

practiceProblems.title: Ransom Note
practiceProblems.description: Check if ransom note can be constructed from magazine letters.
practiceProblems.solution: Count magazine letters. Decrement for ransom note. If any count < 0, impossible.

practiceProblems.title: Jewels and Stones
practiceProblems.description: Count how many stones are jewels (jewels are characters in J).
practiceProblems.solution: Hash set of jewels. Count stones in set.

practiceProblems.title: Uncommon Words from Two Sentences
practiceProblems.description: Find words that appear exactly once in either sentence.
practiceProblems.example: s1='this apple is sweet', s2='this apple is sour'. Output: ['sweet','sour']
practiceProblems.solution: Hash map: word → count. Count words from both sentences. Return words with count 1.

Two Sum
Longest Consecutive Sequence
snippets.code:
def longest_consecutive(nums):
    num_set = set(nums)
    longest = 0
    
    for num in num_set:
        if num - 1 not in num_set:  # Start of sequence
            current = num
            streak = 1
            while current + 1 in num_set:
                current += 1
                streak += 1
            longest = max(longest, streak)
    
    return longest  # O(n) time
